target_customer: Mobile phone users who wanted free messaging between phones and computers
problem: SMS cost money and mobile IM was clunky. Heysan bridged IM and SMS with free messaging and a mobile community.
business_model: free consumer mobile messaging with no clear revenue model

founders.name: Gustaf Alstromer
founders.background_notes: YC page: now a General Partner at YC.

founders.name: Parham Michael Ossareh
founders.background_notes: Listed as tech dude on the YC page.

competitors.name: Meebo
competitors.what: Web access to MSN, AIM and Gtalk that inspired the mobile version

technical_complexity.rationale: Bridging IM networks and SMS across carriers and handsets in 2007 required messaging integration and many device clients.

defensibility.rationale: No proprietary data or network; smartphones and later apps replaced mobile IM bridges.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Good Technology acquired Heysan in May 2009 per the YC page; deal terms not found.

market_need_then: A 2007 review cited M:Metrics data that 6.3 percent of US mobile subscribers used mobile IM versus 41.1 percent who sent SMS, showing paid SMS dominated.

branding.community_and_virality: Reviewed on WAP Review in 2007; the YC page says it built a mobile community of over a million users.

brand_strength.rationale: Reached over a million users per the YC page but little brand coverage was found.

pivots.from: free messaging between phones and computers
pivots.why: YC page says the service expanded into launching a mobile community; reason not stated.

outcome_analysis: Heysan joined YC in Winter 2007, raised a seed round from Khosla Ventures and Atomico that summer, and grew past one million users, then was acquired by Good Technology in May 2009. Terms are not public, the product disappeared, and smartphone messaging apps soon made SMS bridges less relevant, so the outcome looks like a modest acquisition.
notes: No company website listed in the directory (dead or none). Seed amount not found; SeedTable lists 20K dated 2007-01 which conflicts with the YC summer 2007 timing and is not recorded. Good Technology deal in May 2009 is stated only on the YC page; search found the similar Intercasting acquisition by Good the same month, so the Heysan deal is not independently confirmed. The 2007-06 seed date is an approximate month from the YC page's summer 2007. Founder education and employers not found. Meebo is named as inspiration, not as a funded rival. Brattberg later employer Recorded Future is a later role, not recorded as a prior employer.
